title: Sunny and the Lyrebird | Bedtime Story
description: Sonny the Quokka hears what sounds like five different birds singing at once from a moonlit clearing and creeps closer to find a single lyrebird, singing every song the bush knows by heart. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
Sunny heard five birds singing at once.

Or so she thought.

She crept toward the sound — careful, quiet, moving through the moonlit understorey without snapping a single twig. The sound grew louder. Then she emerged at the edge of a small clearing and stopped.

One bird.

A lyrebird, standing in the moonlit clearing, its magnificent tail spread wide behind it like a fan of silver lace. And from its throat came everything — a cascade of calls, one flowing into the next without pause. A whipbird. A currawong. The slow tapping of a woodpecker. The rush of water. Something so sweet and clear she didn't recognise it at all.

The lyrebird was alone, but the clearing was full of sound.

Sunny sat very still at the edge of the trees.

The lyrebird sang and turned slowly, its tail fanning the moonlight. It was performing for no one — or perhaps for everything — for the trees, for the dark sky, for the memory of every sound it had ever heard.

She thought: it has listened so carefully to the whole world that it can give it all back.

The lyrebird called something soft and high. Then something rolling and low. Then nothing — it stood in silence for a long moment, tail still fanned.

Then it folded its tail, stepped quietly into the shadow, and was gone.

Sunny sat in the empty clearing, which somehow still felt full.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, lyrebird. Goodnight, little one.
